source.caption: Fig. 4. Identification of the bacterial mixtures. (a-c) LDA for the binary and (d-f) ternary bacterial mixtures of P. aeruginosa, E. coli, E. sakazakii, S. typhimurium, L. monocytogenes and S. aureus.

source.text: Six LDA score plots (Factor 2 vs Factor 1) for discriminating bacterial mixtures. Panels a–c show binary mixtures at 1:1, 1:4 and 1:8 ratios (P. aeruginosa:S. aureus, E. coli:L. monocytogenes, E. sakazakii:S. typhimurium) together with the pure species and a blank. Panels d–f show different combinations of two- and three-species mixtures. In every panel each group of about five replicate points sits inside its own coloured confidence ellipse, and no ellipses overlap. Factor 1 explains 99.2–99.9% of the variance and Factor 2 explains 0.1–0.7%. In the binary panels the mixture clusters lie between the two pure species along Factor 1, moving toward the second species as its proportion increases.
